title: Inbox command
description: inbox/<ulid>.json: one command from the owner (CLI, Herald, lite phone client), or from the Chancellor's office (source = chancellor: its triage of memos, PS-03b; an amendment's author, PS-22b), or from the temple (source = monk: the Monk's temple_report, PS-12c), waiting for the Steward, the single writer of quest state (ADR 0005). The Steward applies commands in id order at the start of every tick, appends command.applied or command.rejected, and moves the file to inbox/done/. Idempotent: a command id that already has a command.applied event is skipped. Kinds match the design's action icons (seal, return, summon, suspend, reassign, archive, temple, declare) plus the lifecycle commands the state machine needs.
$comment: Generated by `pnpm schemas` from the zod source in packages/domain/src/schema (ADR 0003): change the zod source, never this file. One oneOf branch per kind: each fixes `kind` and gives its payload. confirm (draft -> open) and edit_quest (`elvaria quest edit`) are additions to the plan's §2.3 list, required by the single-writer rule; pin_tag (pin a character to an expertise tag, product plan 0.5 §6) was added with plan 0.5; set_level (the owner sets a character's level) and create_quest's assignee with P1-29, confirm's assignee (`elvaria quest confirm --to`) after it; set_model (the owner moves a character to another model of its tribe) with P1-22; decide_memo (the owner closes a memo) with PS-02; escalate_memo (the Chancellor's triage sends a memo to the owner), source = chancellor, and the memos of create_quest and edit_quest with PS-03b; decide_amendment (an amendment's author decided it, source = chancellor) with PS-22b; deliver (the owner asks the Steward to deliver a done quest's branch to its forge again, after a delivery.failed or to find its pull request anew) with PS-08c; hold and unhold (the owner holds an open or claimed quest, which the Steward then neither claims nor starts, and lifts the hold) and submit (the owner sends the work a quest in the infirmary holds to review, same run) with fix/quest-hold; patrol (the owner asks the Steward to patrol a territory's default branch now, `elvaria territory patrol --now`, as after fixing it by hand) with PS-09d; report_escape (the owner reports a defect that escaped with a quest already in its base branch, `elvaria quest escaped`, a quest and a note as seal takes) and resume_delegation (the owner resumes a territory's delegation of the seal that the breaker suspended, `elvaria territory delegation --resume`) with PS-08g; temple_report (the Monk's operations on single lines of scripture and its letters, source = monk; the Steward checks each before it writes) with PS-12c. archive covers discard (draft), reject (awaiting_seal) and archive (done, infirmary); the Steward picks the transition from the quest's current status. edit_quest is rejected when the quest's updated_at differs from expected_updated_at.

assignee.description: The character the owner gives the draft to as it opens (`elvaria quest confirm --to`): the Steward checks it as create_quest's assignee and gives it the quest in the same apply, before any tick could claim the quest for another. The Steward refuses the command, leaving the draft as it is, when the character is unknown, of another class, suspended or of a disabled tribe. Absent: the Steward picks, as before.

payload.description: Return always carries a note (design: the Return button requires one). The Steward writes it as the owner's fail verdict, which needs notes of at least 20 characters and a fail_kind (`other` when absent).

rejudge.description: The judge erred, not the assignee (P1-40): the owner's verdict says `rejudge`, and the return counts in neither the assignee's reputation nor its fail streak. Absent: false.

payload.description: 'I signed in again': probe this tribe now.
Without character, the Steward selects the next eligible character.
draft = true when it comes from the Chancellor (quest starts in `draft`, needs confirm); false for `elvaria quest add` (starts `open`). The Steward writes the quest file.

party_role.description: Set when this plan quest forms a party (product plan 0.5 §6). Parts come later from the party lead's output, the merge quest from the Steward; neither goes through the inbox.

scope_paths.description: The files the quest changes, as globs relative to the territory root (`packages/domain/src/dispatch/**`). Within a territory the Steward never starts a quest whose scope meets the scope a quest holds (from its first run until it is archived, waiting for the owner's merge included), unless its plot is built on that quest's branch; a session-tier quest without a scope runs alone among working quests. Files the work changes outside the scope go into the `quest.submitted` line and the judge's prompt, never an automatic fail. Hot files every branch edits belong in territory.shared_paths, not here.

question.description: The Chancellor's one follow-up question; the draft is created with blocked.question.

memos.description: The memos the quest is made from (PS-03b): `elvaria say --memo`, or the Chancellor's triage. Created open, the Steward closes those still open as handled by it; created as a draft, when the owner confirms it.

assignee.description: The character the owner gives the quest to (`elvaria quest add --to`, P1-29): only it takes the quest, as after a reassign naming it; its level aside, a rank above its ceiling makes the quest wait for the royal seal. Only for a session-tier quest created open (draft = false). The Steward refuses the command, creating no quest, when the character is unknown, of another class, suspended or of a disabled tribe.

payload.description: Pin a character to an expertise tag (it ranks first and gives the title); tag = null removes the pin.

The owner sets a character's level (`elvaria character level`), any number of levels up or down. The Steward writes it with level_since = now, so levelChange counts only the verdicts after it, and appends character.level_up or character.level_down as the owner's. Refused when the character already has that level.

The owner moves a character to another model of its own tribe (`elvaria character model`, P1-22): its next session runs it, and the mana gauges of that model bind it. Class, tribe, level and reputation stay. The Steward appends character.model_changed as the owner's. Refused when the character already runs that model, or when its tribe does not serve it (an account with named pools serves the models a pool claims; a one-pool account, the family of the character's model).

The owner decides a memo once (PS-02, ADR 0024; `elvaria memo decide`): set it aside (shelved), refuse it (rejected), or name the quest that does the work (handled). The Steward closes the memo and appends memo.closed. Refused when the memo is unknown or already closed, or the quest unknown. A memo is never answered, and closing it changes no quest. With source = chancellor (PS-03b), the Chancellor's triage sets a memo aside within kingdom.delegation; the line's actor is then the Chancellor.

quest.description: With decision = handled: the quest that does the work.

payload.description: The Chancellor's triage sends a memo to the owner with its advice (PS-03b; source = chancellor): kingdom.delegation does not let the world decide it. The Steward writes the advice as the memo's `escalation` and appends memo.escalated; the memo stays open for the owner and the digest. Refused when the memo is unknown, closed or already sent up.

quest.description: merge: the open quest; new_quest: the draft quest made for the owner to confirm.

payload.description: An amendment's author decided it (PS-22b, ADR 0024; source = chancellor: the Chancellor's office, whether the Chancellor or the mage of the quest's plan spoke): accepted rewrites the quest's description and adds the memo's refs outside its scope_paths to them (a quest with none stays unbounded), while no session holds the quest, and closes the memo; rejected closes it; both let the quest that waits on it go on, the note as the answer to its doer. owner sends it to the owner with the note and holds: the memo stays open and the quest asks the owner. The lines' actor is the memo's author. Refused when the memo is unknown, closed or sent up already, or not an amendment to an author.

note.description: The author's why: the doer's next session reads it as the answer.

description.description: accepted: the quest's description rewritten, whole.

expected_updated_at.description: With description: the quest's updated_at the author read; a quest changed since keeps its own.

payload.description: The Monk's answer to the repeated failures (PS-12c, ADR 0027; source = monk): operations on single lines of scripture, applied in order, and letters. The Steward refuses the whole report (replaces_scripture) when it adds more than TEMPLE_ADDS_MAX (3) lines, the replacing line of a merge included, or takes out of one file more than half the Monk's lines there (never fewer than 2). Else each operation is applied or refused on its own (lesson.added, lesson.retired, lesson.refused): no source verdict, a verdict that is not a fail, an unknown line, a line not the Monk's, the 41st line a session would load, a line the lint refuses or that a redaction pattern matches, a sentence already there. Each letter becomes a proposal memo from the Monk, to the Chancellor or, for a stronger model, to the owner, with an id made from its verdict's quest and its text, so a report applied again files nothing twice.
